title: Load test plan + game day execution for hot-route capacity protection
creator: Talia Benson
description: Define concrete load test scenarios + success criteria to validate hot-route capacity protection (tier-aware rate limits/quotas, priority routing, admission control, controlled shedding) and coordinate execution of an on-call style game day. Deliverables: written test plan, schedule/roles, dashboard checklist, success/failure criteria, and post-exercise follow-ups.
content:
## Context
We’re rolling out hot-route capacity protection to prevent fleet-wide degradation caused by overload on a small number of high-traffic, high-SLA routes (e.g. /v1/chat/completions, embeddings, rerank). Before GA, we need a repeatable load test plan and a game day that simulates realistic enterprise + best-effort traffic under pressure and verifies:

- Enterprise traffic maintains SLO-aligned latency/availability during regional or fleet pressure.
- Best-effort traffic is throttled earlier and predictably (consistent 429 semantics).
- Routing/runtime receive clear capacity signals (queue depth, scheduler lag) to avoid cascading failure.
- Observability + runbooks are sufficient for on-call to diagnose/mitigate.

## Scope
### In scope
- Load generation plans for: baseline, burst, sustained overload, and mixed-workload shapes.
- Success/failure criteria tied to SLOs and protection behavior.
- Game day coordination: schedule, roles, comms, go/no-go gates, and rollback triggers.
- Validation checklist: dashboards, alerts, incident-bot notifications, and 429 payload/header behavior.

### Out of scope
- Full fairness scheduler validation beyond the integration points/signals being added.
- Billing/pricing changes (only metadata hooks are being added elsewhere).

## Preconditions / setup
1) Feature flags and allowlists ready for canary region:
   - hot_route_protection_enabled
   - tier_aware_rate_limits_enabled
   - priority_routing_enabled
   - admission_control_capacity_signals_enabled

2) Route groups configured (MVP):
   - /v1/chat/completions (stream + non-stream)
   - /v1/embeddings
   - /v1/rerank

3) Test tenants:
   - Enterprise test tenant (priority class: enterprise)
   - Best-effort/self-serve test tenant (priority class: best_effort)

4) Observability present in target region(s):
   - Per-route/per-tier request volume, p50/p95/p99 latency
   - 429 counts by reason (quota vs overload admission vs overload shed)
   - Shed rate and admission decisions by tier
   - Runtime queue depth and scheduler lag signals
   - 5xx error rate + saturation signals (GPU utilization, scheduler backlog)

## Tools
- Primary load generator: internal loadgen harness (preferred for auth + realistic payloads)
- Backup: k6 scripts for deterministic step ramps and streaming coverage
- Traffic capture: sampled request shapes from route inventory doc (sequence length distributions)

## Scenarios
We will run each scenario with a fixed model/version pinned (to reduce variability) and repeat runs with two workload mixes:
- Mix A: short prompts (low context), higher RPS
- Mix B: long prompts (high context), lower RPS but heavier tokens/s

### S0: Baseline (no pressure)
Goal: establish baseline latency and error rates with protections enabled.
- Duration: 15 min steady-state
- Expected:
  - Enterprise and best-effort have similar latency distributions (within normal variance)
  - 429s ~= 0 (except explicit quota tests)
  - No shed events

### S1: Burst on hot route (chat)
Goal: simulate a “noisy neighbor” burst and validate best-effort gating first.
- Pattern:
  - Enterprise: steady load (representing committed capacity)
  - Best-effort: step increase to 3–5x baseline over 2 minutes, hold 10 minutes
- Expected:
  - Enterprise p95 latency stays within enterprise SLO target for the route
  - Best-effort gets 429s earlier than enterprise and with stable semantics
  - 5xx does not spike fleet-wide; no sustained tail-latency collapse

### S2: Sustained overload with mixed routes
Goal: simulate pressure across multiple hot routes and ensure routing priorities and budgets behave.
- Pattern:
  - Enterprise: steady traffic across chat + embeddings
  - Best-effort: ramp across embeddings + rerank (representing background batch jobs)
  - Total load drives queue depth above the admission threshold for >= 10 minutes
- Expected:
  - Admission control engages for best-effort first
  - Shed reasons tagged correctly (admission vs shed vs quota)
  - Enterprise budget preserved (enterprise admission rate remains high)

### S3: Long-prompt stress test (scheduler lag)
Goal: validate capacity signals for long prompts don’t cause false positives/oscillation.
- Pattern:
  - Introduce long-context requests (p95 context length from inventory doc) on best-effort
  - Keep enterprise short-context steady
- Expected:
  - Thresholds don’t oscillate; we do not flap between admit/shed every few seconds
  - Enterprise p99 remains bounded (no runaway tail)
  - Metrics remain low-cardinality (no explosion in tags)

### S4: 429 semantics validation (client experience)
Goal: ensure consistent error payload and headers for customers/support.
- Execute:
  - Explicit quota exceed (known small quota window)
  - Overload admission control (best-effort)
  - Controlled shedding (best-effort)
- Expected (for all 429s):
  - Response includes machine-parseable reason code and retry guidance
  - Headers present and consistent:
    - x-redwood-429-reason: quota_exceeded | overload_admission | overload_shed
    - retry-after or x-redwood-retry-after-ms
    - request-id / trace correlation header

## Acceptance criteria (pass/fail)
### Must pass
- Enterprise route SLO adherence during S1 and S2:
  - No sustained (>5 min) enterprise p95 breach; no sustained error-rate breach attributable to overload.
- Best-effort protection behavior:
  - Best-effort 429s increase as load increases; enterprise 429s remain near baseline.
  - No “silent” degradation where best-effort is accepted but causes fleet p99 collapse.
- No cascading failure:
  - Fleet 5xx does not spike above defined paging threshold during planned overload.
  - Queue depth and scheduler lag are visible and correlate with admission control behavior.
- Observability + ops readiness:
  - Dashboard panels populate; incident-bot notification fires on protection activation.
  - On-call can answer: “who is being throttled, why, and what lever to pull” within 10 minutes.

### Fail criteria (stop test / rollback)
- Enterprise route p95 breaches for >5 min AND correlates with best-effort not being gated.
- 5xx error rate increases to Sev2 paging level (or higher) during test window.
- Metric-cardinality blow-up detected (e.g., new tags from shed reason dimensions).
- Any auth/tenant isolation anomaly in debug tooling or logs.

## Game day execution plan
### Timing
- Dry run: staging (or shadow prod) 2026-01-13
- Game day: prod canary region (us-east) 2026-01-16, 10:00–11:30 PT

### Roles
- Game day lead / incident commander: Rafael Mendes
- Traffic driver / loadgen operator: Aisha Bello
- Routing observer: Mina Haddad / Elena Popov
- Gateway + 429 semantics observer: Amara Diallo
- Runtime signal observer: Sofia Ivanova / Julian Moore
- Infra/fleet observer: Vanessa Ortiz / Keiko Yamamoto
- Scribe: Peter Holtz

### Comms
- Slack: #incidents (simulated incident thread), #eng-sre, #eng-platform
- incident-bot: confirm structured activation messages with dashboard/runbook links

### Checklist (T-30)
- Confirm flags/allowlists in region
- Confirm dashboard links + SLO burn alerts muted/unmuted appropriately for planned exercise
- Confirm rollback plan and owner (Benji Okafor on standby)
- Confirm support comms stance (no external comms; internal-only)

### During exercise
- Treat as a real incident: create a single thread, time-stamp key events, call out mitigations
- Declare “protection engaged” when:
  - admission control state flips to ON for best-effort and shed rate exceeds threshold
- If fail criteria hits, stop load, roll flags back, and document the failure mode

## Artifacts / links
- Confluence game day plan (canonical): sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/game-day-plan-hot-route-overload-simulation.json
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dashboard-spec-hot-route-protection.json
- Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-overload-protection-and-admission-control.json
- MVP scope notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/hot-route-protection-mvp-scope-wip.json

## Post-game-day deliverables
- Summary write-up (what happened, what we learned, what to change)
- List of action items with owners + target dates (file under ENG-4931)
- Threshold adjustments proposal (if needed) + rollout gates for eu-west

## Notes / open questions
- Confirm enterprise SLO numbers used for pass/fail are aligned to latest SLO doc (Sergio / Allison to confirm) before running prod canary.
- Confirm whether streaming termination semantics are validated in S4 for both gateway-terminated and runtime-terminated shedding paths.
comments: 2025-12-10 — Rafael Mendes: Drafted scenario list (S0–S4) and proposed pass/fail criteria. Need final enterprise SLO thresholds per route before we lock numbers. @Sergio Costa can you confirm what we’re using for chat vs embeddings for MVP?

2025-12-11 — Sergio Costa: SLO targets are in the enterprise-route tiers doc; for MVP we’re using route-specific p95 latency + availability. I’ll add the exact thresholds as annotations in the dashboard so the game day checklist can reference them directly.

2025-12-12 — Amara Diallo: For S4, please validate both header + JSON body fields. We’ve standardized reason codes but need to ensure streaming path also includes the termination marker. I’ll provide example curl outputs once PR-27441 is merged to canary.

2025-12-16 — Sofia Ivanova: Long-prompt stress (S3) is important; scheduler lag can look “healthy” on GPU util but still cause tail blowups. Please include queue_depth AND scheduler_lag panels as primary signals, and we should capture token/s and inflight requests too.

2026-01-07 — Aisha Bello: Loadgen scripts ready for chat + embeddings. Need confirmation on the allowlisted tenants and tokens for enterprise vs best-effort. Also need a dedicated window to avoid overlapping with release train (checking with #eng-releases).

2026-01-09 — Benji Okafor: Rollback plan: single flag hot_route_protection_enabled is sufficient to revert to legacy throttling path in canary, but only if config migration (ENG-27512) has completed. I’ll be on standby during the exercise.

2026-01-13 — Peter Holtz (scribe): Dry run in staging completed. Observed expected best-effort admission gating, but we saw metric-tag cardinality creep when we included customer_id in an overload event dimension. Filed follow-up to remove/aggregate (already tracked under ENG-4925/PR-27488).

2026-01-16 — Rafael Mendes: Game day executed in us-east canary. Results: enterprise p95 stayed within target during burst; best-effort 429s increased with overload_admission reason; no fleet-wide 5xx spike. One issue: rerank route shed reasons were missing for ~6% of 429s (header present, body missing). Adding follow-up under ENG-4931.

2026-01-23 — Rafael Mendes: Closed out ticket with post-game-day summary and action items filed. Biggest wins: clear correlation between queue depth and admission control; incident-bot messages were actionable. Remaining risk: threshold tuning for long-prompt mix in eu-west; to be addressed before regional rollout.
